title: cli-retry: Wire cmd_retry to lifecycle::retry (currently no-op)
description: Bug P0-2. lifecycle::retry at crates/vb_cli/src/lifecycle.rs:235-302 is a fully implemented retry primitive that opens the Fjall journal, computes the new state, and writes JournalEvent::RunRetried. But run_ops.rs:24-98 (cmd_retry) only calls commands_journal::analyze_retry (a pure read-only check) and returns; grep across crates/vb_cli/src for `lifecycle::|crate::lifecycle` outside lifecycle.rs itself returns zero call sites. cmd_retry is a no-op. Worse, analyze_retry (commands_journal.rs:348) sets can_retry: true unconditionally for RunCancelled runs, allowing retry of a cancelled run which violates master §44.19 (typed and graceful failure of validation/compile/runtime/storage/IPC/action/replay). Master §33.3 (Lifecycle Command Surface) lists retry as a first-class command. This bead: (1) imports crate::lifecycle in run_ops.rs and calls lifecycle::retry after analyze_retry confirms can_retry: true; (2) fixes analyze_retry to set can_retry: false when run is in RunCancelled terminal state.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a JournalEvent::RunRetried when cmd_retry is invoked on a retryable run
THE SYSTEM SHALL reject retry of a RunCancelled run with a typed CancelledRunNotRetryable error

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb retry <run-id> --db <path>` on a run in RunFailed state
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL open the Fjall journal, call lifecycle::retry, and append JournalEvent::RunRetried

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb retry <run-id> --db <path>` on a run in RunCancelled state
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 3 with CancelledRunNotRetryable and write nothing to the journal

unwanted.condition: IF cmd_retry is called on a non-existent run id
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT create a journal entry or silently exit 0
unwanted.because: Operators must be told the run id is wrong; silent success masks operator error

unwanted.condition: IF cmd_retry is called on a run already in RunRetried state
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT stack multiple retried events on the same run
unwanted.because: Each retry must be a single explicit operator action; idempotency here would hide double-clicks

preconditions: Run exists in the Fjall journal at the supplied --db path
Run is in a retryable terminal state: RunFailed OR (post-fix: not RunCancelled)
postconditions: JournalEvent::RunRetried is appended with the original run_id and a fresh attempt_seq
Run's step states are reset to Pending for the failed steps only; succeeded steps remain Succeeded (lifecycle::retry preserves progress)
invariants: Retried runs retain all prior journal events (append-only, never truncate)
lifecycle::retry is called via the `crate::lifecycle` module path; no duplicate implementations are introduced

happy: cli_retry_after_failed_run_writes_run_retried_event: submit a run that fails, then `vb retry <id> --db /tmp/db`; journal contains JournalEvent::RunRetried with the original run_id
cli_retry_preserves_succeeded_steps: run a 5-step workflow that fails at step 3, retry; steps 1-2 are still Succeeded, step 3 is Pending
error: cli_retry_after_cancelled_run_returns_cancelled_error: cancel a run, then retry; exits 3 with `CancelledRunNotRetryable`

Does analyze_retry's fix need to thread to analyze_resume's can_resume logic too? (Yes for state-driven consistency; P0-3 covers the resume side.)

security_failures.failure: Operator retries a run that contains a Secret-tainted slot, leaking the secret into the new attempt's journal
security_failures.prevention: lifecycle::retry reuses the existing RunState (which already carries the taint array); new attempt inherits the same secret taint, no extra write

usability_failures.failure: Operator sees a successful `vb retry` exit but no journal event was written
usability_failures.prevention: cmd_retry must verify the journal write succeeded (Fjall commit acked) before exiting 0

data_integrity_failures.failure: lifecycle::retry is called twice on the same failed run, creating two Retried events and double-counting attempts
data_integrity_failures.prevention: analyze_retry must check current run state; once in RunRetried, can_retry: false

integration_failures.failure: vb retry on a run owned by a different shard fails because run_ops.rs has no shard routing
integration_failures.prevention: Pass run_id through to lifecycle::retry which already routes via Shard::enqueue

Read crates/vb_cli/src/commands/journal.rs:348 (analyze_retry) and the surrounding RunState matching arms
phase_1: Write test test_cli_retry_after_failed_run_writes_run_retried_event (submit+fail a workflow, then retry, scan journal for RunRetried)
Write test test_cli_retry_after_cancelled_run_returns_cancelled_error (cancel, then retry, assert exit 3 and CancelledRunNotRetryable)
phase_2: In run_ops.rs:24-98 cmd_retry, add `use crate::lifecycle;` import
In cmd_retry, after `analyze_retry` confirms can_retry: true, open the Fjall journal (using the existing open_journal helper) and call `lifecycle::retry(parse_run_id(run_id), &journal)?`
In commands/journal.rs:348 analyze_retry, add a match arm for RunState::RunCancelled that sets can_retry: false and reason: 'RunCancelled; not retryable'
phase_3: Update the cmd_retry --help text to mention the cancelled-run rejection
phase_4: Run `moon run :test -p vb_cli` and verify all new tests pass
